title: Proton pump inhibitors and risk of gastric cancer: population-based cohort study
authors: Abrahami D, McDonald EG, Schnitzer ME, Barkun AN, Suissa S, Azoulay L
population: UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink new users of PPIs (n = 973,281) or H2-receptor antagonists (n = 193,306), 1990 to April 2018; new-user active-comparator design
funder: Not read: the publisher page refused access and the article is not in PubMed Central; PubMed lists Canadian Institutes of Health Research grant FDN-143328.
authorConflicts: SS participated in advisory meetings or as guest speaker for Atara Biotherapeutics, Boehringer-Ingelheim, Bristol-Myers-Squibb, Merck and Pfizer; LA served as consultant for Janssen and Pfizer, all unrelated to the study (abstract record).
result: Against H2-receptor antagonists, PPI use HR 1.45 (95% CI 1.06 to 1.98) for gastric cancer; number needed to harm 2121 at 5 years and 1191 at 10 years after treatment initiation. HRs increased with cumulative duration, cumulative omeprazole equivalents and time since initiation; results were consistent across sensitivity analyses.
